## Pull request overview

Implements remaining Console roadmap P0/P1 spec-compliance items by extending the ListView schema/behavior (row height, conditional formatting, inline edit, ARIA, sharing) and adding view-specific rendering support to `NavigationOverlay`.

**Changes:**
- Extend `ListViewSchema` with spec-aligned properties (`rowHeight`, `conditionalFormatting`, `inlineEdit`, `aria`, `sharing`) and add a shared conditional-formatting evaluator.
- Update `ListView` to map `rowHeight` → density mode, forward `inlineEdit`/`conditionalFormatting` to the grid schema, apply ARIA attributes, and show a Share button when enabled.
- Add `renderView` to `NavigationOverlay` (with tests) and update roadmap checkboxes.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 7 out of 7 changed files in this pull request and generated 7 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/types/src/objectql.ts | Adds new ListView spec properties to the public TypeScript contract. |
| packages/plugin-list/src/index.tsx | Re-exports `evaluateConditionalFormatting` from the plugin entrypoint. |
| packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx | Implements rowHeight→density mapping, exports conditional formatting evaluator, forwards props to grid, adds ARIA + Share UI. |
| packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListView.test.tsx | Adds tests for rowHeight mapping, density precedence, ARIA, and sharing button rendering. |
| packages/components/src/custom/navigation-overlay.tsx | Adds `renderView` prop and prioritizes it when `view` is provided. |
| packages/components/src/__tests__/navigation-overlay.test.tsx | Adds coverage for `renderView` behavior and fallback logic. |
| ROADMAP.md | Marks several roadmap items as completed. |
</details>

The new `evaluateConditionalFormatting()` helper is exported as part of the public plugin API but isn’t covered by tests. Adding unit tests for each operator (equals/not_equals/contains/greater_than/less_than/in) and for the “first match wins” behavior would help prevent regressions as child views start relying on it.

The Share button’s visible text is hidden on small screens (`hidden sm:inline`), leaving only an icon + `title`. Since `title` is not a reliable accessible name, the control can become unlabeled for screen readers. Consider adding an explicit `aria-label` (or an `sr-only` label) so it remains accessible at all breakpoints.

`ListViewSchema` is being extended with new spec properties (rowHeight/conditionalFormatting/inlineEdit/aria/sharing). The repo also maintains Zod runtime validators advertised as “complete” (`packages/types/src/zod/README.md`), but `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` currently defines `ListViewSchema` with only objectName/viewType/fields/filters/sort/options. Consider updating the Zod `ListViewSchema` to validate these new properties (enums/shape), so runtime validation and docs stay aligned with the TypeScript types.

ROADMAP/PR description mark `exportOptions` as complete for csv/xlsx/json/pdf, but `ListView`’s export handler currently only implements CSV and JSON (no XLSX/PDF generation). Either implement the missing formats or adjust the roadmap/description so it matches current behavior.

The root container is always given role="region", but when `schema.aria.label` is not provided this creates an unnamed landmark region (discouraged and can add noise for screen readers). Consider only setting `role="region"` when a label/labelledby is available, or derive a default accessible name (e.g., from `schema.label`/`objectName`) when enabling the region role.

`rowHeight` is mapped into a `density` state, but that density result is only used for the toolbar button label/cycle and is not applied to the rendered view (nor forwarded to the child grid). As a result, setting `schema.rowHeight`/`densityMode` won’t actually change row/cell spacing. Consider forwarding `rowHeight` to `object-grid` (it already supports compact/medium/tall) and/or using `density.paddingClass`/`density.fontSizeClass` to affect the rendered content.

`conditionalFormatting` is forwarded into the `object-grid` schema, but the current `ObjectGrid` implementation doesn’t read or apply any `conditionalFormatting` prop, so this feature will have no effect in grid view. Either wire these rules into `ObjectGrid`/`data-table` (e.g., compute row/cell styles via `evaluateConditionalFormatting`) or avoid forwarding until there’s a consumer to prevent a false sense of support.
